expectations.evidence: Recommends 'KubeVirt on RKE2 Government' with a detailed alternatives comparison table (Proxmox, OpenStack, Nutanix AHV, Harvester) including pros, cons, and verdicts. ADR-001 provides full rationale.

Section 8 'Air-Gapped Operations Model' covers artifact transfer process with encrypted USB/data diode, disconnected registry (Harbor), disconnected RPM repos (Satellite/Pulp), offline Kubernetes operations (RKE2 air-gap bundles, offline Helm charts), and patch management cadence.

Section 7.1 maps IL5 security controls to implementations across NIST 800-53 control families (AC, AU, CM, IA, IR, SC, SI) and mandates FIPS 140-2 cryptography. Section 7.4 details encryption architecture for data at rest and in transit with FIPS compliance.

Section 10 'ATO Maintenance Plan' covers security impact analysis, modified ATO process, RMF artifacts to update (SSP, SCA, POA&M, PPS, etc.), STIG mapping from VMware to K8s equivalents, and a continuous authorization (cATO) path.

Section 9.1 defines 5 migration waves (Wave 0 pilot through Wave 4) over 16-20 weeks with specific VM counts, categories, risk levels, and durations. Section 9.2 details per-VM migration phases (Assessment, Preparation, Execution, Validation & Cutover).

Section 9.5 lists specific tools: qemu-img for VMDK-to-qcow2 conversion, ovftool for vSphere export, CDI (Containerized Data Importer) for importing into PVCs, virtctl for image upload. Section 6.4 shows the conversion pipeline: VMDK -> qcow2 -> KubeVirt CDI import.

Section 7.2 details STIG compliance for RHEL OS (DISA RHEL STIG via OpenSCAP + Ansible), Kubernetes (DISA Kubernetes STIG, RKE2 CIS-hardened), container images (DISA Container STIG, Iron Bank), and Windows VMs (DISA Windows Server STIG). Section 10.3 maps VMware STIGs to KubeVirt/K8s equivalents.

Section 8.2 covers Harbor as the disconnected registry with Iron Bank image mirroring via transfer media, Helm chart storage, offline Trivy DB updates, and inter-cluster replication. Kyverno policy in Section 7.5 enforces all images originate from local Harbor.

Section 6 covers Rook-Ceph with RBD (replicated and erasure-coded pools) for VM disks, CephFS for shared filesystems, RGW for object storage. Includes storage classes with YAML examples, sizing tables, and NVMe vs SSD tiering.

Section 9.6 'Rollback Strategy' states vSphere VMs are not decommissioned until 72 hours of successful production on KubeVirt, failed VMs revert to original vSphere VM, DNS/LB changes are easily reversible, and all manifests are in Git for clean rollback.
